KINES 500: This course provides a foundational overview of evidence-based practice (EBP) in the health sciences, which includes an overview of the seven steps of the EBP process.
KINES 530: Research techniques, including methods, research design, techniques for data collection, as applied to relevant problems in Kinesiology.
KINES 531: Analysis of professional/academic issues related to athletic training; includes medical considerations, legal and professional developments, and current research.
KINES 540: This seminar explores the literature, methodologies, theoretical challenges, and research questions confronting the field.
KINES 551: The course will address contemporary theories and methods in motor control as reflected in recently published scientific papers.
KINES 565: The basic understanding of neurophysiological structures and mechanisms involved in the generation of human voluntary movement.
KINES 566: Basic concepts and principles of psychophysiology and their application for analyses of human movements.
KINES 567: Physiological changes during exercise with emphasis on the effects of physical conditioning and training.
KINES 575: Introduces the theory and practice behind the primary experimental methods used in biomechanics and motor control.
KINES 577: In-depth study of the heart and circulatory system with emphasis on the effects of exercise on cardiovascular function.
KINES 579: Biomechanical foundation of human movement and injury prevention.
KINES 588: Instruct students in writing grant proposals, abstracts, manuscripts, and effective presentations in their respective scientific fields of study in Kinesology.
KINES 590: Continuing seminars which consist of a series of individual lectures by faculty, students or outside speakers.
KINES 590B: Continuing colloquia in exercise physiology which consists of individual lectures by outside speakers, students and faculty.
KINES 594: Supervised student activities on research projects identified on an individual or small-group basis.
KINES 596: Creative projects, nonthesis research, which are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
KINES 597: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject that may be topical or of special interest.
KINES 602: Preparation and presentation of materials in lecture and laboratory classes under the supervision of a full time faculty member.
